quote_text:
Today, the support—you could see  it was a dedicated performance. 
At times, it feels like 30 [years] to be fair, but  you can't ask for a lot more than that. For me,  
it’s an extension of our performances. You  know, we’ve been good, and you don’t get the  
credit when you lose — obviously, emotions  are high. We’ve played very well in the last  
three games. I believe we’ve been better than  Hearts and Hibs in the performances. Today,  
we got our rewards, and we’ve raised the  expectations at this football club now.
It’s not been because we’ve got massive  resources or an injection of cash — it’s  
because of the squad of players, and they deserve  every amount of credit for the performance.
You brought on Jonah and Toyosi  Alusanya — that clearly worked. 
Yeah, we thought Jonah would give us a  platform in the game — and I thought he  
did. He held the ball up, allowed us to  get a bit of ownership, because you can’t  
come to Ibrox and defend for 96 minutes. We  certainly weren’t going to plan to do that.
Then, when the game opened up, Toyosi’s  pace — we really felt — would hurt them,  
which it proved. You don’t always get  these things right, but, on paper,  
it sounded good today and it worked on the park.
The biggest thing was we didn’t feel  under pressure. You come to these places,  
and a lot of times, you don’t have  ownership of the game. We felt we  
were in control when we landed on the  ball. We were really brave and created  
lots of half-chances — perhaps  could’ve scored a couple more.
You seemed unusually bullish  before the game — was there  
something that gave you that confidence? I must’ve been in a good mood. I don’t  
know why — I’d just been for a run  with the staff, that’s probably why!
But I’ll be honest with you, I always  fancy my chances everywhere I go because  
I know how hard the staff and the players  work on their shape. There are teams in this  
division that sit in and play on the counter,  but we go aggressive. We press, and we press  
aggressively. You can’t do it for 90 minutes,  but when we go, we go together as a team.
You always feel that if you can  silence a crowd for 45 minutes,  
it gives you an opportunity. That’s what  happened. Then Rangers have to come out and  
be a bit more expansive, and it leaves gaps  in behind. We’ve got players we believe can  
hurt people. Toyosi is unbelievable off the  bench at times, though I start him a lot too.
The expectation now is that they don’t fear  anyone — and that’s a testament to the players.
Did you see Rangers’ vulnerability this afternoon? 
Look, we’ll talk all about Rangers — but I just  want to talk about St Mirren. It’s not my job to  
talk about Rangers — that’s Philippe’s job. My  job is to acknowledge a very good performance.
We sensed we were in control of the  game. When we landed on the ball,  
we kept it well and got it to the other  side of the pitch. We were clinical, took  
our chances when they came, and didn’t  feel we were under a lot of threat.
We’ve got three clean sheets in six now — and  that’s the key to winning football matches.
When it went to 2-0, did you expect a more  
robust challenge? A late Rangers  onslaught that just didn’t come? 
You know, I believe that’s credit to the  St Mirren players. I’m not going to say  
anything bad about Rangers — that’s not my  job. My opinion on Rangers doesn’t matter.
My opinion on us is that we had a game  plan, we were very good at carrying it out,  
and we’ve been very good for a period  of time without getting those headline  
results. We got that today — through  hard work, endeavor, and quality.
We have a big game Wednesday night.
A lot of teams that come here sit deep, defend in  numbers — I didn’t see that from St Mirren today.  
I saw you being aggressive with a high line  and a good press. That must have pleased you. 
Yeah, you probably don’t see us every week,  but we do press aggressively every week. We  
don’t change that when we come to the  bigger clubs. You might take your line  
slightly deeper to start your press, but  we’ve got legs and energy in the team.
The players are the ones who have to do that. I  can set them up with all sorts of tactical ideas,  
but they deserve every amount of  credit. They ran over Rangers at  
times. Their pressing and quality when  they landed on the ball was a joy to watch.
When you see a group of boys who  don’t get paid millions of pounds  
and just go and try to win every single  game — you can’t help but admire that.  
You’ll have bad times, of course, but I  have to give them all the credit I can.
Does this kind of performance push you towards the  
top six split? Can you keep pushing for that? Yeah, we know we’ve got four games before the  
split — and the next two are vital. We play teams  in and around us. Nothing will be settled today.
What we said was: we’re under no pressure.  There are teams with resources way beyond  
our imagination fighting for this top  six. If we were to get there three years  
in a row, it would be a massive  overachievement for this group.
We’ve not had an individual investor, we’ve  not had millions thrown at us — we’ve just  
tried to grow the club slowly and  prudently. Now, there are six games  
to go. Any St Mirren manager in the last 40  years would have snapped your hand off for  
this chance. I’ll get credit for it — yes  — but the players deserve every bit of it.
It’s the first win at Ibrox  since 1981 — and back-to-back  
wins over Rangers for the first time in 45 years.  Was that the challenge you set the players? 
We’ve set the challenge across the  next three games. Everyone said,  
“Look, you’ve got Rangers, Hearts, and Celtic  — last year’s top three. You’ll get nothing.”
But we have a belief within ourselves. If we press  properly, land on the ball, and — the thing that’s  
been missing — if we’re clinical enough in both  boxes, we can hurt teams. We did that today.
We don’t talk about incentives of beating  Rangers. My sole focus is on St Mirren.  
You can’t worry about records. Somebody else  can talk about records — that’s their job. My  
job is to try and win every game. You can’t do  that all the time, but you have to set out to.
Your thoughts on the potential  red card? It happened so quickly. 
Did I think it was a red card? It’s not for  me to suggest that other players should get  
sent off. VAR looked at it and decided  it wasn’t. It didn’t impact the game,  
so I’d be wrong to comment without  seeing a proper replay. We’ve only got  
one slow-motion replay, so it’s  wrong for me to comment on that.
Thanks, Stephen.
title: Stephen Robinson Post Match Interview | Rangers 0-2 St Mirren
